items.q: Does TrendFit upload my health data?
items.a: No. TrendFit reads Apple HealthKit data locally on your device. Your data is never uploaded, shared, or sold — ever.

items.q: What health data does TrendFit access?
items.a: TrendFit reads workout data (active energy, heart rate, pace, duration, distance and similar workout metrics), personal metrics (age, gender, height, weight), and — from version 2.0 — workout routes, which TrendFitGroup uses to recognise repeated routes. Access is read-only: TrendFit has no permission to write to Health at all. Version 2.0 also removed 15 data types the app was not using, so it asks for less than it did before.

items.q: Does TrendFit use any third-party services?
items.a: No third-party services process or store your HealthKit data. All analysis happens on-device. Cloudflare Web Analytics is used on this website (not in the app) to count page visits — no personal data is collected.
No. TrendFit is for informational purposes only and is not a substitute for medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.
iPhone running iOS 18.0 or later, with Apple Health permissions granted. TrendFitGroup additionally needs outdoor workouts that recorded a GPS route. The app is English-only.
Open TrendFit and follow the onboarding prompt to grant HealthKit read access. You can adjust permissions at any time in Settings → Privacy & Security → Health.
TrendFit is free on the App Store. Search for "TrendFit" or use the Download button on the home page.
TrendFit answers one question per mode. TrendFit itself asks whether a single metric is improving over time — pick an activity and a metric, and it draws the trend line through your history.
TrendFitStack puts several activities on one chart so you can see how they divide the work between them, and can draw each calendar year as its own line for a like-for-like comparison.

New in 2.0. TrendFitGroup matches outdoor workouts that followed the same GPS route and charts your pace, speed and duration across every repeat of it, so you can see whether you are getting faster on the routes you actually run.
TrendFitChallenge lets you set a target and a deadline, then projects whether you are on course for it from the work you have already done.

items.q: What do the red, yellow, and green trend lines mean?
items.a: The color reflects the direction the trend line visibly moves on the chart. Green means the trend is improving, red means it is declining, and yellow means the line is roughly flat in the current view. For metrics where lower is better — like pace and heart rate — the colors are interpreted accordingly, so a falling pace line shows green. The color always matches the line you see, at any zoom level.

items.q: Can I zoom and pan the charts?
items.a: Yes. Pinch to zoom into any timeframe, then swipe to pan through your full history. Tap any data point for exact numbers.

items.q: Can I personalise units and chart windows?
items.a: Yes. You can set metric or imperial units, choose your chart lookback window — 3, 6, 12, 24 or 36 months — and configure haptic feedback from the app settings.

For cumulative metrics (energy, distance) TrendFit projects a scaled total from your HealthKit history. For rate-based metrics (heart rate, pace, cadence) it suggests your historical average as the target.

items.q: Can I edit or delete a challenge?
items.a: Yes. In-progress challenge targets and durations are editable (with a confirmation step). Challenges can also be deleted — a confirmation is required before anything is removed.

TrendFit sends optional local push notifications for challenge progress. You can configure the frequency in App Settings (daily, every 3 days, weekly, or a custom interval). All notifications are generated on-device — nothing is sent to external servers.
